canonical_data: Kernel configurations, plugins and kernel functions, prompt templates, agent definitions, chat-history threads, process definitions, and records in connected vector stores
current_repo_note: The README (fetched 2026-08-29) opens with an important notice: "Semantic Kernel is now Microsoft Agent Framework!" It describes Microsoft Agent Framework as "the enterprise-ready successor to Semantic Kernel," now at a production-ready 1.0 with stable APIs and long-term support, and points readers to a Semantic Kernel migration guide. Unlike AutoGen, the README carries no maintenance-mode notice and the repository still received commits on 2026-08-27.
strengths: Genuinely multi-language rather than a Python project with ports: maintained Python, .NET, and Java trees in one repository with published PyPI and NuGet packages and per-language API references

A wide substitutable integration surface — OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Hugging Face, and NVIDIA NIM backends plus documented local execution through Ollama, LM Studio, and ONNX, alongside Azure AI Search, Chroma, Elasticsearch, Qdrant, Postgres, Redis, Pinecone, MongoDB, Weaviate, and FAISS connectors

Explicit developer control surfaces: typed kernel functions, OpenAPI and MCP plugins, function-choice behavior, filters, reliability policies, structured output through Pydantic models, and the Process Framework for modeling business workflows
weaknesses: Microsoft has declared it superseded: the README's first line states Semantic Kernel "is now Microsoft Agent Framework" and names that project the enterprise-ready successor, so new work is steered away from this SDK even though commits continue

The successor announcement is not paired with a stated support horizon in the repository, so adopters cannot tell from authoritative repository sources how long Semantic Kernel will keep receiving fixes
Feature parity differs by language, which is why the project maintains a separate supported-languages feature matrix; a capability demonstrated in the Python samples is not guaranteed in .NET or Java
Quickstarts, samples, and defaults are Azure-first, so the model-agnostic design takes more work to realize outside the Azure OpenAI path
why_it_matters: Semantic Kernel is the enterprise-facing half of the lineage that Microsoft consolidated into Microsoft Agent Framework, and it is the framework that carried plugin-based agent orchestration into .NET and Java shops; recording it as superseded preserves that reach while pointing adopters at the maintained path.
